title: Two-word keys (A+B and sandwich A+B+A, repeating, every phase, L 4-26) on one hidden alphabet: true Quagmire III (C = P + K, P - K, K - P), true Quagmire II, and idea 93's numeric one-alphabet model (repeating and sliding), joined through the forced key slots and solved exactly
k4_result: 4,987 cells (2,666 pair + 2,321 sandwich; cell = form, L, split, phase). Before any word is used, true Quagmire III C = P + K and C = P - K are impossible in every cell, for ANY key of period 4-26: a forced-different pair of clue places always lands on the same key slot (it stays impossible up to period 26; the first live periods are 27-30, 41, 53+). C = K - P is dead in 4,003 of 4,987 cells, Quagmire II in 2,155. The rest: 21.35M joined pairs solved exactly (24 equations mod 26, letters in distinct places), 5.2e11 word-pair settings decided by the joins. Located models (Quagmire III/II): 0 survivors. Numeric models: 22 survivors, all with nonsense keys (MPE+AQHOUSE, TYSEV+OUTLOOK, RNERANDT+LCSINVERT ...); best reading with 15+ quadgrams outside the clues scores -7.43 on the big model (word cover 0.35), and none reads as English (0 above -5.1).
controls: 3 shuffled K4s, a sixth of the cells each (cells 0::6, 1::6, 2::6), same tiers and caps: 0, 2 and 0 survivors; best reading -7.87 (gibberish); 0 readable. For shuffled texts Quagmire III C = P + K is not dead at every period (478-719 of ~830 cells dead), so the blanket kill is specific to K4's letters.
planted: 5/5 in the full run (SHADOW+FORCES Quagmire III C = K - P L 12; BERLIN+WALL Quagmire III C = P + K L 10; sandwich EAST+BERLIN+EAST Quagmire II L 14; CLOCK+WISE numeric sliding L 9; sandwich LAYER+TWO+LAYER numeric on KRYPTOS values L 13): each found among 3,000 decoy words, alphabet recovered, 73-88 of 97 letters read back, English -4.37 to -5.34
scope_limits: Key lengths 4-26 only (pair: both words 2+ letters; sandwich 2a+b <= 26); the plan's sliding form only for the numeric models (for true Quagmire III/II a sliding key's conditions are linear in the alphabet, not letter conditions, so they do not split by word). Vocabulary is tiered per cell to fit 30 minutes: located models solve at most 15,000 joined pairs per cell, taking the first tier under that cap: big x big (264,828 words and K1-K3 windows) / big x common / common x common (37,896) / theme x common (85 theme words). For K4, C = K - P cells: 217 big, 1 mixed, 331 common, 433 theme, 2 skipped; Quagmire II: 563 big, 34 mixed, 477 common, 1,710 theme, 48 skipped (L 16, 19, 23). Numeric models: common x common (else theme x common) under a cap of 4,000 per model/valuation/kind; 782 and 545 repeating-key cells fell to the theme tier. So most Quagmire II and many Beaufort-type cells are covered only for pairs that include a theme word. Not covered: three or more words, words outside the lists, German, Quagmire IV (two alphabets), keys longer than 26. The clue positions are taken as exact. Controls ran on a sixth of the cells each, not all cells.

negative.family: Word key on a hidden tableau
negative.hypothesis: K4's key is two remembered words written one after the other (A+B, or A+B+A), repeating, on one hidden alphabet (true Quagmire III or II, or a numeric key on one hidden alphabet).
negative.scope: Pair keys L 4-26 and sandwich keys 2a+b <= 26, every split and phase (4,987 cells); true Quagmire III (C = P + K, P - K, K - P) and Quagmire II (plain on A-Z or KRYPTOS) with repeating keys; one hidden alphabet with key values on A-Z or KRYPTOS (C = P + k, C = k - P), repeating and sliding. Words from 264,828 (big), 37,896 (common) and 85 (theme) lists, tiered per cell under caps of 15,000 (located) and 4,000 (numeric) joined pairs; joins on the forced-equal / forced-different key slots and on the fixed dot products; exact solve mod 26 with distinct places.
negative.outcome: Dead in scope: Quagmire III C = P + K and C = P - K are impossible at every period 4-26 whatever the key; across all models 21.35M joined pairs solved, 22 numeric survivors, none readable (best -7.43); 0 located survivors (controls, a sixth of cells each: 0, 2, 0 survivors, best -7.87, none readable; planted 5/5 found and read back).

follow_ups: True Quagmire III C = P + K / P - K first comes alive at periods 27-30 and 41. A known-word test there (one word of 27-30 letters is rare, so two or three words joined as here) is the only place left for that model with a repeating key.

Raise the caps for Quagmire II (1,710 K4 cells fell to theme x common) with a stronger split filter: for Quagmire II each side's own equations already fix part of the hidden alphabet, so a canonical form of the A-side partial solution could replace the bit-mask join.

Sliding keys on true Quagmire III with two words: the forced-equal pairs become 'the alphabet places of a stretch of key letters sum to 0 mod 26'. That is linear and could be joined over the letter-count vectors of each word.
